comparisons.peer_summary: AMD returned $862 million to shareholders in 2024 through stock repurchases, with $4.7 billion remaining available under a program that has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose shareholder return mechanisms and their discretionary nature, but AMD focuses on stock repurchases while NVDA focuses on cash dividends. AMD explicitly states its repurchase program 'may be suspended or discontinued at any time' and has no termination date, reflecting similar discretionary governance to NVDA's statement that the dividend program is subject to the Board's 'continuing determination.' However, the financial mechanisms differ: AMD returned $862 million via share repurchases in 2024, whereas NVDA's disclosure focuses on the governance of its cash dividend program rather than specific payout amounts in this snippet.

sentences.text: Our cash dividend program and the payment of future cash dividends under that program are subject to our Board of Directors' continuing determination that the dividend program and the declaration of dividends thereunder are in the best interests of our shareholders.
The stock repurchase program does not obligate us to acquire any common stock, has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.
